learned_patterns.pattern: A full 7-day gap (07-01 through 07-06) passed with no CLU session and no fresh Signal Engine run, so ledger grading (INTC/ARKK/NVDA windows), the Wed/Fri projected_journey updates, and DRIP ex-date timing all lapsed. The scheduled-automation layer is the single point of failure — when it stops firing, the whole cadence silently stalls and the account runs unmanaged between the last session and the next manual invocation.

The Signal Engine has not produced a fresh matrix since 06-30 12:21 PDT. SAFE MODE has now persisted for over a week. The §2.5 staleness guard is doing its job (no trades on week-old signals), but the root cause — the workflow_dispatch Signal Engine not being fired before sessions — makes CLU unable to take any signal-based action. Top operational fix.

The tech/semi pullback (-4.5% book over the gap; SOXX -9%, INTC -8.5%) is exactly the scenario CORE's no-stop design is built for: broad ETFs are not stopped out on drawdowns (§13), so the pullback is absorbed as future reinvestment rather than realized as forced exits. Only the LAB single-stock stops (all intact) carry downside triggers.

The 06-30 matrix showed composites NEUTRAL/BEARISH even as prices ripped into quarter-end; a week later prices have reverted down toward those bearish composites. The lagging MACD-driven composite that looked 'wrong' at the top was directionally early on the reversal — weak confirmation, but a reminder not to fight a BEARISH composite (NVDA -0.338) with price euphoria.

Allocation holds near target at LAB 25.6% / CORE 49.8% / DRIP 24.1% without any trade — the pullback shrank LAB/CORE and left DRIP slightly heavier, keeping DRIP the most-underweight tier (-5.9pp) and the next-deposit target. Passive drift plus the JEPQ seed keeps the glide path roughly on track between deposits.
